brief.recommendation: Checkout at 0% success (120/120 failed) vs 95% SLO, $18,400/min revenue at risk [BIZ-4], exceeding 60s tolerance [BIZ-1]. Blocker tmp_orders_backfill_v2 not in workload registry (owner/cost unknown) [BIZ-2], so interrupt cost unquantifiable [BIZ-5, I4]. No protected settlements [DB-2] or change-calendar protection [BIZ-3]. Historical precedent shows terminating similar batch_worker jobs restored checkout to 100% within 10s [MEM-1], but this exact workload is unvetted. Per I4, human owner must decide.

audit.report: Checkout degraded to 0% success (120/120 failed over 30s) against a 95% SLO, putting $18,400/min of revenue at risk and exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance. The root blocker was pid 1278248, a tmp_orders_backfill_v2 batch worker idle in transaction for 4.2 seconds with last statement SELECT 1, holding locks that blocked 12 checkout sessions. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, citing severe business impact and historical precedent for similar batch workers. The Continuity Guardian escalated to on-call because Invariant I4 was violated: tmp_orders_backfill_v2 is not in the workload registry, so its interrupt cost could not be priced and automatic termination was not permitted. No remediation action was executed; the incident remained escalated at 245 seconds with one negotiation round completed.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered tmp_orders_backfill_v2 batch worker held order-table locks while idle in transaction, blocking checkout and triggering an Invariant I4 escalation that prevented automatic termination.
lessons: Register tmp_orders_backfill_v2 in the workload registry with owner, interrupt cost, and priority metadata so future incidents can be auto-resolved without human escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified the blocker and proposed termination based on measured 0% checkout success and $18,400/min revenue at risk, but the Continuity Guardian properly invoked Invariant I4 to block termination of an unregistered workload whose interrupt cost was unquantifiable, forcing human escalation.
follow_ups: Register tmp_orders_backfill_v2 in the workload registry with owner, cost, and priority metadata within 24 hours.
Audit all batch workers for registry compliance and add idle-in-transaction timeouts on order-table access.
Define an on-call response SLA for Invariant I4 escalations to prevent 245-second stalls during checkout outages.
